diagnostic_evidence.quote: By a similar reasoning, $\kappa=0$ is always an eigenvalue for any $n$, since we may choose $v\equiv w$ to be any harmonic function on $D$, again without imposing any boundary conditions.

issues.failure_explanation: The paper concludes that 0 is in the continuous spectrum of the ITP from the fact that harmonic functions v≡w give infinitely many eigenfunctions at κ=0. Under the standard classification invoked by the citation, a value with a nontrivial kernel belongs to the point spectrum (here an eigenvalue of infinite multiplicity and an accumulation point of the eigenvalues); the continuous spectrum consists of non-eigenvalue spectral values. The inference drawn in the sentence is therefore invalid, and the stated classification is false as written.

failure_location.quote: we conclude that $0$ belongs to the \emph{continuous spectrum} of the ITP \cite{Kubrusly2012}

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace 'continuous spectrum' by 'point spectrum of infinite multiplicity' (or 'accumulation point of the ITEs'); no other change is needed.
issues.overall_effect: Only the motivational classification of κ=0 in the setup is wrong; no labelled result, algorithm, or guarantee depends on it (κ=0 is excluded from the analysis regardless).
issues.title: Zero ITE misclassified as belonging to the continuous spectrum
issues.why_classification: A one-word terminology correction; the exclusion of κ=0 and all subsequent results are unaffected.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Then $p=p^\star$ gives rise to an exceptional point, since the eigenpair trajectory is non-differentiable there.

issues.failure_explanation: The final step lets p→p* in the one-sided identity and needs the integral ∫(v'·conj(v)−n·conj(w)·w') to stay bounded. The theorem assumes continuous differentiability only on the punctured interval, which does not bound the derivatives as p→p*; boundedness would follow only from C¹ regularity up to p*, i.e. from the negation of (part of) the conclusion. Moreover, even read as a proof by contradiction, the computation only rules out continuous differentiability at p*, whereas the statement claims the (stronger) non-differentiability of the trajectory.

failure_location.quote: because the integral factor stays bounded as a consequence of the continuous differentiability of the eigenfunction trajectory near $p^\star$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the limit argument by a pointwise one: assume for contradiction that the trajectory is differentiable at p*, differentiate the identity \eqref{eq:ibp} in p at p*, and use κ*∈ℝ (so Im(κ*²)=0) together with I(p*)=0, which follows from one-sided continuity of I and Lemma lem:zeronorm; this yields 0 = ½κ*²∫n'|w|², contradicting κ*≠0 and ∫n'|w|²≠0. This both closes the inference gap and proves genuine non-differentiability.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem thm:bifurc's stated conclusion (non-differentiability at p*) is not established by its proof; only non-C¹-smoothness is supported. cor:bifurc is not affected (it follows from the pointwise identity at p* alone), and the propositions only assert that the results 'apply'.
issues.title: Proof of Theorem thm:bifurc uses an unestablished boundedness and yields less than 'non-differentiable'
issues.why_classification: The repair is a short, local, routine pointwise-differentiation argument at p* replacing the flawed limit step; the theorem's conclusion (exceptional point, non-differentiability) is fully preserved and no other labelled result depends on the flawed step.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Therein, we observe that the indicator becomes positive if and only if an eigenvalue trajectory is (i) real and (ii) traveling to the right.
although now all bifurcations are cubic and the indicator $\overline{I}$ is uniformly non-positive.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose repeatedly describes the plotted simplified indicator with the sign opposite to the paper's own formulas. By eq:ind_simpl, \overline{I} = 2I/(a_mπ(1−p²)); for p>1 this prefactor is negative, so sign(\overline{I}) = −sign(I). On the disk, the proof of prop:disk:bifurc gives I(p) = (a_mπ/2)(1−p²)|α|²J_m(κ_p)², hence \overline{I} = |α|²J_m(κ_p)² ≥ 0 for real trajectories: the prose claim that the indicator is 'strictly negative' for real disk curves (and the caption '\overline{I}(p)∼−|p−p*|^α', and 'uniformly non-positive' for the disk) is impossible. On the annulus, eq:bifurc_ord with n'_p = 2p > 0 and κ_p > 0 gives sign(κ') = sign(I) = −sign(\overline{I}), so \overline{I} > 0 corresponds to LEFTWARD travel; the prose asserts the opposite ('positive if and only if (i) real and (ii) traveling to the right') and asserts this is 'confirmed' by cor:bifurc/lem:bifurc_ord, which actually yields the opposite sign relation. One single sign convention cannot satisfy both the formulas and the prose.

failure_location.quote: On the other hand, the indicator is strictly negative for real eigenvalue curves, except at bifurcation points, in agreement with \cref{cor:bifurc}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Flip the sign consistently in one place: either correct the prose/figure descriptions (indicator positive for leftward-traveling real branches, non-negative on the disk), or redefine \overline{I} with prefactor 2/(a_mπ(p²−1)) and adjust the statement of prop:annulus:bifurc_ord accordingly; no proof or theorem needs to change.
issues.overall_effect: The interpretation of the indicator plots (figs. disk_ind, annulus_ind, annuluslarge_ind, annuluslarge_ind_zoom, annulusdisk_ind), the fitted-rate captions ('\overline{I}(p)∼−|p−p*|^α'), and the claimed theoretical confirmations of the sign behaviour are unreliable as described; the formal results (eq:bifurc_ord, prop:annulus:bifurc_ord, cor:bifurc_sufficient) themselves remain valid.
issues.title: Simplified indicator described with the opposite sign to the paper's own formulas
issues.why_classification: A local sign flip in the descriptions (or in the plotted quantity) restores consistency; every rate estimate, bifurcation order, and theorem is unaffected.

issues.failure_explanation: By prop:annulus:bifurc_ord the bifurcation criterion is \|v_p\|_{L^∞(∂B_1)} = r\|v_p\|_{L^∞(∂B_r)}, i.e., for the separable form v = f(ρ)φ(mθ) (eq:annulus:functions) it reads |f(1)|² = r²|f(r)|². The boundary L²-norms satisfy ‖v_p‖²_{L²(∂B_1)} = a_mπ|f(1)|² and ‖v_p‖²_{L²(∂B_r)} = a_mπ r |f_v(r)|² (surface measure), so the criterion is equivalent to ‖v_p‖²_{L²(∂B_1)} = r ‖v_p‖²_{L²(∂B_r)}, i.e. ‖v_p‖_{L²(∂B_1)} = √r ‖v_p‖_{L²(∂B_r)} (or, with the unweighted dθ convention, ‖v_p‖_{L²(∂B_1)} = r ‖v_p‖_{L²(∂B_r)}); under either convention equality of the two L² norms holds only for r = 1, which is excluded.

failure_location.quote: By the assumed polar-coordinate separability in \cref{eq:annulus:functions}, this is actually equivalent to $\|v_p\|_{L^2(\partial B_1)}=\|v_p\|_{L^2(\partial B_r)}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert the missing factor, e.g. state the criterion as ‖v_p‖_{L²(∂B_1)} = √r ‖v_p‖_{L²(∂B_r)} (surface measure); a local one-line correction.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised practical criterion for detecting annulus bifurcations via boundary L² norms is wrong as stated (missing factor √r, or r under the dθ convention); prop:annulus:bifurc_ord itself is unaffected.
issues.title: Annulus bifurcation criterion in L² norms drops a factor of r
issues.why_classification: A routine local correction of the equivalence restores the criterion; no proof, rate, or result depends on the erroneous form.
